dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you?

Yes. Hello. My name is Priya Okafor. I am calling about the storm drain at the corner by my house. It backed up in the storm, and my basement took water. And I want somebody to come look at it. Today, if possible.
Okay, I'm sorry to hear that. Let me get some information. What's the address?
Thirty-one Howard Street. In the Fifth Ward. The drain is at the corner, maybe, eh, four houses down from me. On the same side.
Thirty-one Howard. Okay. And this was from the storm over the weekend, Friday into Saturday?

Yes. Overnight Friday into Saturday. Saturday the tenth. I went down in the morning, around six, and there is water on the floor. About three inches. I measured with the ruler, so I am not guessing. Three inches.
Three inches. And do you know how it got in?

Two places. The window well on the street side, the glass. The water filled up the well outside and came through around the glass. And the bulkhead door. Under it, at the bottom. So both of these, the street side.
Okay, window well glass on the street side and the bulkhead. Got it.

And I want to tell you also. Friday night, before it came in, I looked out the window. The manhole near the corner, the cover, water was bubbling up through it. Coming up out of the street. Like a pot. So the water has nowhere to go, it comes up, and it runs down the street to my house. This is not the rain falling on my house. This is the drain.
The manhole was bubbling up. That's helpful, I'll put that in, because that tells them it's the line and not just the grate.

[pause] Yes, well. The grate also. I will be honest with you. That grate is covered with leaves since October. Every day I walk past. Leaves, sand, a coffee cup. Nobody comes to clean it. I see the street sweeper go by in the fall, it goes around the corner and that grate, nothing. So then the big storm comes and of course. Of course it backs up. Anybody could tell you this would happen.
I hear you. I'll note the grate's been covered with debris too.

Please note it. Because now I have the mess and it is two days and nobody has come. The manhole was doing this Friday night. The whole neighborhood can see it. And still nobody from the city is on the street. I thought maybe somebody would drive by Saturday and look. No.
After that storm, honestly, the crews were out on everything all weekend, but that doesn't help you, I know. What got damaged down there?

Paint cans. Ladders. Those were on the floor along the wall, so now the ladders are standing in water, the paint cans are rusting on the bottom, the labels came off. And boxes. Boxes of my kids' school things. Old papers, report cards, drawings, the things you keep. Cardboard boxes, on the floor. They are wet through, the bottoms. I have them on the table now to dry but [pause] some of it is finished. You can't fix wet paper.
Oh, that's the stuff you can't replace. I'm sorry.

Yes. Well. So I want a crew to come and check the drain and clear it. Right away. Not next week. Because the weather they say more rain later in the week, and if this drain is still blocked, it does the same thing again and I am back in the basement with the bucket.

Understood. Okay, so I'm logging this as a drain backup at the corner by thirty-one Howard, manhole surcharging, water into the basement. Let me look at the board here. [pause] Today they've got everybody tied up on the storm work, there's a list. The soonest I can get a crew to that corner is tomorrow, Tuesday the thirteenth.
Tomorrow. [pause] Not today.
Not today, I'm sorry. I'm putting it in for tomorrow, the thirteenth, and I'm flagging that the manhole was bubbling so they know it's not just a leaf problem.
Okay. Tomorrow what time?
Sometime during the day shift, so morning into early afternoon. You don't need to be home for it, they work from the street.
Fine. But I want them to do it properly. Not just take the leaves off the top and drive away. If the water is coming up out of the manhole, something is under there. Somebody has to look under.
I'll write that exactly. Check the line under the corner, not just the grate.
Thank you. Write it, please. Because I know how this goes. Somebody comes, five minutes, they sweep, they leave.
It's in there. Can I get a phone number for you, in case there's any follow-up on this?
Yes. Four oh one, five five five, oh one four oh. That is my cell.
Four oh one, five five five, zero one four zero. And it's Priya, P-R-I-Y-A?
Yes. And Okafor, O-K-A-F-O-R.

O-K-A-F-O-R. Perfect. And for the damage to your things, if you want to put in a claim with the city, that's a separate thing, I can tell you who handles that, or you can check with your homeowner's insurance first, whichever you'd like.

I will think about it. Today I just want the water to stop coming. My sister is driving down from Tiverton this afternoon to help me carry the boxes out and pull up what is wet. She is not happy, she has to drive in this. But okay. Two old women with a wet-vac. [pause] It should not be like this when the drain is right there.
I know. Hopefully tomorrow they get it running so you're not doing this again.
Hopefully. So tomorrow, the thirteenth. If nobody comes, I call you back.
Call us back, absolutely. Ask for Public Works and reference the drain backup at thirty-one Howard, it'll come right up.
Okay. Thank you, Denise.
You're welcome. Good luck with the cleanup, and tell your sister to drive careful.
I will. Goodbye.
